children: The Netherlands’ trade surplus widened to EUR 10.9 billion in July 2026 from EUR 9.0 billion in the same month a year earlier.
Exports rose 13.6% year-on-year to EUR 75.2 billion, driven by higher shipments to both the EU (+9.2%) and non-EU countries (+12.5%).

Among commodities, outbound shipments increased the most for animal and vegetable oils and fats (+33.3%), machinery and equipment (+26.3%), mineral fuels and lubricants (+20.2%), and chemical products (+15.9%).
Meanwhile, imports grew 8.9% to EUR 62.2 billion, lifted by increased purchases from both the EU (+7.5%) and non-EU countries (+10.2%).
Import growth was supported by machinery and equipment (+19.5%), animal and vegetable oils and fats (+19.4%), mineral fuels and lubricants (+12.7%), and beverages and tobacco (+12.7%).
In the January–July period, the Dutch trade surplus stood at EUR 67.0 billion, as exports rose 5.6%, while imports grew 4.8%.

title: Dutch Trade Surplus Widens in July
